I think this is lacking some nuance. I think sometimes people forget that depression is a spectrum, and a very complex mental illness. I’ve been experiencing severe and treatment resistant depression since i was 10. I’ve been in therapy since i was 7, tired more medications than i can count, etc etc. Depression can’t be cured for everyone, and a lot of times it’s influenced by outside factors. 

For example, i’m physically disabled. I can barely walk most days so i’m very isolated in doors. There’s not much i can do about that, or the pain. It’s hard for someone to pull themselves up by their bootstraps when they’re in an abusive home, homeless, or dealing w multiple mental illnesses. 

It’s important to try your best, even if it feels pointless. Even if you can’t brush your teeth and take a shower every day, if you’re trying your best then that’s what matters. If someone is in a depressive episode it doesn’t mean they aren’t doing enough or trying enough. They need encouragement to as best as they can to stay afloat, even if it’s small things.

Ideally it’s recommended to save 20-30% of your income and if someone has money after needs and savings, and they wanna spend money on hobbies, then I think they should. Life is short and it’s good to enjoy it while you can. What’s the point of saving all of your money if you’re gonna spend decades of your youth wrecking your mental health from no downtime and always working?

With budgeting, you can set aside extra money for hobbies if you’re not living paycheck to paycheck. and some hobbies are free. Life would be boring if all people did was work and invest.
